cover.title: A soldier spoke to her. He died in 1863.

lines.text: In July 1863, more than fifty thousand men were killed, wounded, captured or lost in just three days... and some visitors say a few of them never left.
Gettysburg, Pennsylvania. The bloodiest battle of the American Civil War.
On July second, Confederate troops fought their way into a maze of giant boulders called Devil's Den.
Days later, photographers arrived. One famous picture shows a dead Confederate sharpshooter between the rocks. Historians later found the body had been moved there, for the photo.
Today it's a national park. And the rangers tell a story about Devil's Den.
A visitor said a ragged man in a floppy hat, barefoot, walked up to her and said: what you're looking for is over there. Then he was gone.
The rangers said she'd just described exactly what a Texas soldier looked like in 1863.
If a stranger told you it's over there... would you look? Comment over there, partner.
